strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: clearly articulates the temporal gap between error introduction and observable conflict in incremental graph construction
Comprehensive three-stage framework: coherent pipeline for conflict detection, error localization, and repair with sensible separation of concerns
Solid technical approach: LCA-based divergence tracing and edge impact scoring with interpretable factors (reachability, conflict count, usage)
Thorough ablation studies: detailed component analysis across multiple models (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, Claude-Haiku) in Tables 1-2
Dataset refinement contribution: systematic 5-step pipeline to remove 160 conflicting edges, providing cleaner testbed with conflict distribution analysis
Version control as engineering contribution: novel application of versioned history capture for graph repair with rollback and tracing capabilities
Good related work grounding: appropriate connections to SLAM, knowledge graphs, and scene graphs
weaknesses: Extremely narrow evaluation scope: limited to 53 interactive fiction environments from single MANGO dataset with no evaluation on other spatial domains or graph reasoning tasks; generalizability highly questionable
Modest absolute performance: best accuracy only 54.88% with concerning failure patterns (Edge-Impact Ranking achieves 75% repair rate but only 45% correctness)
Critical evaluation clarity issues: ground truth determination unexplained, reference graphs not discussed, no validation strategy provided for the 160 edge removals from dataset refinement

Heuristic edge impact scoring lacks principled justification: equal weighting after normalization (Eq. 2) appears ad-hoc; PageRank motivation is hand-wavy without rigorous support; no learned weights or sensitivity analysis

Silent error problem fundamentally unresolved: paper acknowledges persistent undetected errors but provides no statistics on false negative rates or method to address them; severely limits practical utility

Weak baseline comparison: Baseline(GPT-4o) achieves only 5.77% accuracy suggesting poorly designed baseline; no comparison to alternative graph repair, optimization, or constraint satisfaction methods

Limited experimental scope: no ablation on individual impact factors, no sensitivity analysis on 10-iteration repair limit, no evaluation on raw (unrefined) MANGO dataset, no statistical significance testing
Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned, exact prompts to GPT-4o not provided, random seed handling not discussed, computational cost of repair not analyzed
Framework generalization unclear: version control and conflict types are task-specific; unclear how approach would adapt to 3D environments, knowledge graphs, or other spatial reasoning domains
Marginal improvement from combining components: Version Control alone achieves 54.00%, combined method 54.88%—only 0.88 percentage point gain despite added complexity

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear articulation of temporal gap between error introduction and conflict manifestation
Comprehensive four-tier evaluation spanning controlled synthetic graphs, cross-vendor testing (7 LLMs), real IF maps, and natural text deployment
Methodologically sound algorithmic validation (Appendix B) separating core algorithm contributions from LLM variability using 1,160 synthetic test cases
Novel technical integration of LCA-based error localization over Reasoning History Tree, providing unified framework for multiple conflict types
Thorough ablation studies (Table 1) clearly demonstrating individual component contributions
Useful dataset contribution: cleaned MANGO variant removing non-topological actions and inconsistencies
Clear presentation with effective visualizations communicating problem space
weaknesses: Severe over-generation in headline result: 4× ground-truth node/edge counts on Dream of the Red Chamber undermines practical utility and contradicts goal of coherent spatial memory

Strong model-dependency without principled solution: optimal configurations differ by model (Table 3), 2 of 7 models show regression (Table 2), proposed held-out validation requires costly LLM inference

Incomplete precision/recall characterization: Table 4 reports only recall; inferred precision ~25% from 4× over-generation unacceptable for structured mapping; Table A3 shows repairs lose 31-89 ground-truth edges indicating problematic trade-off
Severely limited end-to-end evaluation: only Chapters 16-17 of single novel with one repair LLM; authors explicitly acknowledge 'broader literary corpus remains future work'

Minimal baseline comparisons: only simple heuristics; missing comparison to knowledge graph repair, schema-guided error correction, or RAG approaches; heuristic_remove achieves 98 conflicts vs. best LLM at 396-625, challenging LLM repair necessity
Continuous spatial reasoning inadequately addressed: discretization increases false positives, acknowledged but unsolved, severely limiting applicability to natural language

Edge Impact Score lacks theoretical grounding: Equation 2 uses unweighted normalization without justification; perfect Spearman correlation (TC6) on 5-edge sanity-check treated as generalization evidence
Hyperparameter sensitivity: 20-iteration choice driven by volatile 5-game sweep (results: −32.4%, −32.4%, +50.9%, −17.6%); no principled justification for 3 attempts per conflict
Silent errors handled unsystematically: E→J example illustrates issue but framework provides no systematic detection beyond context accumulation
Statistical significance not formally assessed despite modest improvements in many cases and high variance
Version Control computational overhead not quantified; scalability to large graphs not demonstrated
Conflict detection limited to observable violations; cannot detect latent semantic inconsistencies; structurally coherent maps could still be semantically incorrect
